quotes.text: Learn how to accept TWINT, a popular payment method in Switzerland.

old_evidence.text: While Stripe still supports this product, this support might end if the product is deprecated.
You must specify the `return_url`, which redirects the user after they complete the payment.

findings: November's canonical body is only the purpose statement plus Checkout and Direct API variant links and mobile iOS and Android routes (new 5-17). May 3, 2026 is the actual fetch date of its embedded Checkout and Direct API guide (old 2, 8-17 and 121-129). The November mobile links expand navigation and establish neither body content nor fresh SDK support, deprecation or runtime behavior.

In the May one-time Checkout route the merchant enables Dynamic Payment Methods or manually lists TWINT, uses payment mode and CHF for all line items, and the buyer approves through an approved TWINT app. May lists Europe/UK business scope at Checkout. The hosted example uses success_url, embedded_page uses return_url, and the guide refers fulfillment separately (old 12-106).

In May's explicitly legacy and no-longer-recommended Direct API path, the merchant creates a CHF PaymentIntent with TWINT, sends the client secret to the customer-facing client, and uses confirmTwintPayment with required return_url and optional billing details. Stripe.js handles the redirect. In the other server-driven path, the merchant confirms with payment_method_data type twint and follows next_action.redirect_to_url.url if requires_action (old 121-162, 231-285, 291-351).

May test success authenticates at the redirect and transitions requires_action to succeeded. Selecting Fail test payment transitions requires_action to requires_payment_method. On return Stripe appends PaymentIntent ID and client secret for recovery, while the guide warns against merchant logging or embedding the secret and recommends verifying Intent status and listening for payment_intent.succeeded rather than relying on a browser callback (old 250-254, 280-289, 347-357).

Root index line 7 links to Stripe index 283-289 and 753-758, then to the overview/acceptance and TWINT concept. Concept 51-60 links acceptance, save, setup and subscription paths; source 33-35 only routes to the May raw. Keep the old raw and restore a reciprocal TWINT link in the historical source correction.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/twint/accept-a-payment only lists Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android variants. It establishes no integration prerequisites or payment state transition itself (new raw lines 5-17). The May 3, 2026 guide describes a one-time CHF Checkout Session where the customer approves with an approved TWINT app. The manual Checkout illustrations include card and TWINT, while Stripe also documents dynamic presentation. The legacy Direct API uses a server-created CHF PaymentIntent and client-side confirmTwintPayment with required return_url and optional billing details. Stripe.js handles the redirect. On the separate manual server route, requires_action exposes next_action.redirect_to_url.url. May tests move requires_action to succeeded or requires_payment_method, and payment status or a webhook is the fulfillment authority (old raw lines 12-106, old raw lines 121-162 and old raw lines 231-357). source-stripe-twint-accept-payment.md preserves the routes but conflates the two redirect behaviors and needs a dated correction.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/twint/accept-a-payment, the November change is navigation-only. The previous May 3 guide embedded Checkout and legacy Direct API; November links to them and exposes iOS and Android navigation without including variant bodies (old raw lines 8-17 and old raw lines 121-129, new raw lines 9-17). Keep source-stripe-twint-accept-payment.md tied to the May one-time CHF flow, hosted success_url and embedded return_url examples, legacy Stripe.js recommendation and optional server redirect. Keep payment status verification separate from browser return. The general TWINT concept should scope setup-mode and mandate examples to the distinct future-use guides; May’s one-time server example omits mandate_data, and its client helper handles redirects rather than presenting the manual next_action URL (old raw lines 58-102, old raw lines 250-289 and old raw lines 291-357). Preserve raw provenance and the reciprocal TWINT concept and companion guide routes.
